messages.author: 01297f55bb13765d
messages.subject: Suggestions Required
parts:
Sir/Madam,

I'm Sumin George, working in Keystone Fondation based in kotagiri,
Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu, India. We intend to study the bee nest density
in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (NBR) . The NBR has an extent of
5250 sq.km of which the forested area is around 4800sq.km. The bee
species included for the study are Apis dorsata - Giant rock bee,
Apis cerana-cavity nesting, Apis florea - shrub nesting & Triogonna
sp.- stingless bee. The bee species vary in their nesting behavior.

I would like to know if distance has been used in similar kind of
exercise , in terms of laying random transects & scanning through the
study area for these bees. Would if someone could help me out
because its my first study using distance.

Regards
Sumin George,
Keystone Foundation.
